Subject: POC trial planning - model selection and success criteria (recap + next steps)

Thanks again for the call today — great discussion and appreciate the clear goals. I wanted to summarize our notes and propose a concrete plan for the 2-week POC so we can get kickoff scheduled. TL;DR: proposed primary model Llama 2-13B (quantized), fallback Mistral-7B, multilingual evaluation for English/Spanish/Portuguese, 2-week timeline, owners below.

Goals / Success criteria (what Acme needs to see):
- Answer rate >= 85% on the 500 sample queries in Prod-like prompts (English + Spanish + Portuguese)
- Latency: median response < 600ms for baseline queries (95th < 1.5s) on dedicated dev capacity
- Cost: per-request token cost within the budget we discussed (target < $0.015 per 1k tokens across the workload)
- Quality gating: no more than 3% hallucination rate on targeted QA prompts measured by the evaluation template

Evaluation plan:
1) Week 0 (prep, ~3 business days): exchange test corpus + redacted sample data, access + roles, sign SOW. Attach: POC_SOW.pdf and evaluation_template.xlsx.
2) Week 1 (baseline): Spin up trial endpoints, run baseline on primary model (Llama 2-13B quantized). Capture token-level cost, latency, and basic quality metrics.
3) Week 2 (optimization & wrap): Run fallback runs on Mistral-7B for latency-sensitive paths, test prefix-caching and batching config, produce final report and next steps (canary plan or Dedicated quoting).

Model selection rationale:
- Primary: Llama 2-13B (quantized) — good balance of instruction-following quality for multi-turn support and multilingual coverage; straightforward to deploy on your Dedicated or Redwood-hosted trial.
- Fallback: Mistral-7B Instruct — lower latency/cost; used for lower-complexity or high-throughput routes to meet tight SLOs.
- If you need heavier multilingual support we can evaluate an ensemble or a small translation + EN-instruct pipeline, but first-pass we'd run both models on the tri-lingual sample set.

Ownership / stakeholders:
- Marissa Cole (AE) — commercial owner, SOW and scheduling
- Dylan Brooks (Solutions Eng) — technical owner, model tuning, endpoint config, latency testing
- Acme owners: Sofia Morales (product lead), Carlos Vega (platform)

Proposed timeline / next steps:
- Please review and confirm the success criteria above by EOD Friday (Jun 26).
- If agreed, sign the attached POC_SOW and we’ll schedule a 60-min kickoff on Jun 29 to provision endpoints.
- Acme to provide sample test corpus (500 queries) and any restricted data that needs redaction before Jun 26.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite once you confirm.
—

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. We’re aligned on the success criteria overall. A couple of clarifications before we sign: 
1) Latency concerns — our alpha traffic has some sub-second SLA requirements for chat; can you confirm expected median p95 numbers for Llama 2-13B on the trial config? We’d prefer to keep p95 < 1.2s if possible.
2) Multilingual — yes, Spanish and Portuguese are must-haves. We’ll provide ~200 Spanish + 100 Portuguese test queries, plus 200 English. If Llama 2-13B struggles on Portuguese we’re open to the fallback approach.
3) Cost — procurement looped in; can you provide a simple estimate of token cost for the 2-week trial with both models enabled (we’ll send estimated token volumes).

We’ll aim to sign the SOW by Friday if the latency/cost numbers look reasonable. Thanks — Sofia
